questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Ribose, the sugar in RNA, differs from deoxyribose in that ribose has:
questions.explanation: Ribose has an -OH group at the 2'-position of the ring, while deoxyribose has only a -H at that position. This is why RNA is slightly less stable than DNA.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct order of structural hierarchy in proteins from simplest to most complex?
questions.explanation: Proteins are organized into four levels: Primary (amino acid sequence) → Secondary (local folding, helices/sheets) → Tertiary (overall 3D fold) → Quaternary (multi-subunit assembly).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Vitamin K is essential for:
options: Synthesis of clotting factors in the blood
questions.explanation: Vitamin K (phylloquinone) is required for the synthesis of prothrombin and other clotting factors (II, VII, IX, X). Its deficiency causes excessive bleeding.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a fibrous protein?
questions.explanation: Fibrous proteins (e.g., collagen, keratin, myosin) are insoluble structural proteins with elongated shapes. Globular proteins (e.g., insulin, hemoglobin, enzymes) are compact and usually soluble.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What type of hormone is adrenaline (epinephrine)?
questions.explanation: Adrenaline (epinephrine) is an amino acid-derived (catecholamine) hormone derived from tyrosine. It is released from the adrenal medulla during stress.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: RNA differs from DNA structurally in that RNA is usually:
questions.explanation: RNA is generally single-stranded and contains uracil in place of thymine. It also uses a ribose sugar rather than deoxyribose.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The backbone of nucleic acid strands is formed by:
options: Alternating sugar-phosphate units connected by phosphodiester bonds
questions.explanation: The backbone of DNA/RNA consists of alternating pentose sugar and phosphate groups connected by 3',5'-phosphodiester bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Polysaccharides serve as structural material in which of the following organisms?
options: Neither; only proteins serve structural roles
questions.explanation: Cellulose is the structural polysaccharide found in plant cell walls. Chitin is a structural polysaccharide in insects/fungi. Glycogen is a storage, not structural, polysaccharide in animals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which deficiency vitamin causes Beri-beri?
questions.explanation: Deficiency of Vitamin B1 (thiamine) causes Beri-beri, a disease affecting the nervous system and heart. Pellagra is caused by Vitamin B3 deficiency.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Enzymes are denatured at high temperatures because:
options: The active site changes shape due to disruption of weak interactions
Covalent bonds in the backbone rupture
The substrate is also destroyed at high temperature
questions.explanation: High temperatures break weak interactions (H-bonds, hydrophobic, ionic) maintaining the tertiary structure of the enzyme, altering the shape of the active site and causing loss of catalytic activity.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The hormone thyroxine contains which element in addition to C, H, O, N?
questions.explanation: Thyroxine (T4) is a thyroid hormone that contains 4 iodine atoms. It regulates basal metabolic rate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) is a nucleotide of which nitrogenous base?
questions.explanation: ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate) contains adenine as its nitrogenous base. It is the primary energy currency of all living cells.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The hydrolysis of starch first gives which intermediate?
questions.explanation: The hydrolysis of starch proceeds stepwise: starch → dextrins → maltose → glucose. Amylase first breaks starch into dextrins, then into maltose.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following amino acids contains a sulfur atom in its side chain?
questions.explanation: Cysteine (C3H7NO2S) contains a -CH2-SH group in its side chain. It can form disulfide bonds (-S-S-) with other cysteine residues, stabilizing protein structure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: mRNA, tRNA, and rRNA are three types of RNA. Which one carries the genetic message from DNA to the ribosome?
questions.explanation: mRNA (messenger RNA) is transcribed from DNA and carries the genetic code to ribosomes in the cytoplasm for protein synthesis. tRNA brings amino acids, and rRNA forms part of the ribosome structure.
